storyboard: Proto-Industrialisation: Merchant networks in rural cottage industries.
Factory System: Arkwright's mill, Spinning Jenny, hand labor preference.
Colonial India: East India Company's Gomasthas, Manchester cloth influx.
Indian Enterprise: Pioneers (Tagore, Tata, Hukumchand), WWI war supply boom.
summary: Explores industrialization from decentralised rural production to mechanized factories, examining worker resistance and colonial Indian industry.
key_takeaways: Proto-industrial production preceded urban factory systems.
Victorian industrialists favored hand labor due to cheap labor abundance and seasonal needs.
Colonial Gomasthas displaced traditional Indian brokers.
WWI created an industrial boom for Indian cotton and jute mills.
